reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about silicon-rich coatings forming a passivating oxide barrier on boride substrates in molten aluminum, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these key premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover these specific interactions, so the lack of citations leaves the premises entirely unsupported.
premises: Silicon-rich coatings can chemically interact with molten aluminum to form a protective barrier.
The formed barrier reduces direct chemical attack and inhibits aluminum diffusion into the substrate.
The barrier comprises silicon-containing oxides that adhere to the boride substrate.
The protective effect is effective at ~660°C under standard hot-dip conditions.
Untreated boride-based components suffer significant corrosion under these conditions.
